status: measured on exp214 on the real container sound path; no change needed in the product
sign: Positive means sound after the picture, at the browser's estimated audio output time.
correction: An earlier summary said the container path carries no sound. It does: the lab fixture only lacked the session agent and --pcm-fd. Measured here with both, as a user had reported.

stand.chain: ffplay, owned PipeWire, repository qsm-clipboard-agent sound card, audio.sock, the terminal's framing into the worker's --pcm-fd, libopus, TURN over TCP, Chrome 157
stand.server: exp214 in PVE LXC108 with NVENC, H264
stand.stimulus: 1280x720 60 fps moving test picture, a white frame and a 1 kHz tone of 50 ms every 2 s from the same clip clock
stand.receiver: AudioWorklet on the received track; the composed picture read at each animation frame

findings: Direct decode keeps sound 30-46 ms after the picture on an open path and does not drift over 10 minutes. ITU-R BT.1359 puts the detectability limit at 125 ms for late sound and 45 ms for early sound.

At 2 Mbit/s with a full-screen moving picture, direct decode stays closer (-51 ms) than the browser's own path (-184 ms). There sound leads the picture, slightly beyond the 45 ms limit with direct decode and well beyond the 90 ms acceptability limit without it.
After a change of path the offset takes up to about 20-30 s to settle.

At 2 Mbit/s the worker sends about 16-17 frames per second of this synthetic full-screen picture, and 6-10 of the 35 three-frame flashes were not seen. The clip gates use a smaller picture, so they do not cover this case.
limits: One player, ffplay, whose own A-V status read -16 to -28 ms. Other players and browsers in the guest may differ.
The speaker's latency is not included: the stand has a fake audio device reporting 32 ms.
The observer samples the picture at animation frames, so each pair carries about 16 ms of steps.
PVE with NVENC only: the Native lab VM has no audio device, and its path was not measured.
One or two runs per mode. One run's rc=1 was the harness reading ICE statistics at the end; the session had not failed.

exp215_update.note: The full-screen narrow case in the findings above is exp214. With exp215 direct decode keeps sound after the picture there as well.
